newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican peso mixed on pre-weekend swaps.
newsitem.headline: Mexican peso mixed on pre-weekend swaps.

text.p: The Mexican peso ceded some of its initial strength to stand mixed at mid-morning Friday due to swap deals ahead of the weekend, dealers said.
"The market is under a little pressure again. Dealers could be buying dollars to hedge against the outcome of the elections," one dealer said, referring to the July 6 mid-term elections.
The benchmark 48-hour peso was 0.2 of a centavo firmer at 7.9600/7.9630 per dollar, while its 24-hour counterpart was 0.5 of a centavo weaker, respectively, at 7.9570/7.9600 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had meanwhile closed 0.2 of a centavo firmer at 7.9500/7.9520 per dollar.
Traders said dollars were in more demand at 24 hours, as the deals don't have to be paid for until Monday, and in the meantime the pesos can be lucratively invested in the money market.
